chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the man who divorces his wife.
Does he provide her with mut'ah (divorce gift)? He said: 'Yes. Do you not love that you be among the 'Muhsinin' (doers of good)? Do you not love that you be among the 'Muttaqin' (the pious)?'.

key_terms.أَيُمَتِّعُهَا: does he provide her with mut'ah (divorce gift)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on mut'ah in divorce according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the obligation of *mut'ah* (divorce gift) by framing it not merely as a legal transaction but as a means for the husband to attain spiritual ranks. By invoking the qualities of *Muhsinin* (doers of good) and *Muttaqin* (the God-fearing), the Imam connects the material provision to the husband's inner piety and conscious devotion to God. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the spiritual dimension underlying familial legal obligations.
